---
title: "Fixing code and shipping it"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(rewindr)
has_dplyr <- requireNamespace("dplyr", quietly = TRUE)
```

Finding the broken step is half the job. This article covers the other
half: getting a fix, checking that it works, and packaging the result so it
runs anywhere.

## Rule-based fixes (offline)

`suggest_fixes()` turns the issues into code. It needs no network or API
key:

```{r, eval = has_dplyr}
tr <- rewind_script(rewind_example(), key = "order_id")
fx <- suggest_fixes(tr)
knitr::kable(fx[, c("step", "problem")])
cat(fx$suggestion[1])
```

It covers the common silent failures: values that do not parse as numbers
(with real examples of the offending values), join keys that differ by
whitespace or case, duplicated lookup keys, key type mismatches, filters
that drop `NA` rows, and empty results.

## Fixes from Claude

`ask_claude()` sends the recording to the Claude API and gets back a
diagnosis, a list of changes and a complete revised script. You can also
ask for new behaviour in plain English:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
Sys.setenv(ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "...")   # or set it in ~/.Renviron

fix <- ask_claude(tr)                    # fix the detected issues
fix <- ask_claude(tr, "Also fill months with no orders with zero revenue")
fix
```

Nothing runs automatically. Record the revised script and compare it with
the original:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
new <- rewind_script(text = fix$code, key = "order_id")
compare_traces(tr, new)
issues(new)
```

In the app, the **Ask Claude** tab does the same with two buttons.

**What is sent:** the source code, the timeline (one line per step), the
issues, and up to five sample rows from the input and output of each step
that has an issue, plus the join report. Use `max_rows = 0` to send no data
values:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fix <- ask_claude(tr, max_rows = 0)
```

**Model and cost:** the default is `claude-opus-5-5` with adaptive thinking
and `effort = "high"`. Use `effort = "low"` or `"medium"` for faster,
cheaper answers on small scripts, or pass another `model`.

## Compare two runs

`compare_traces()` works for any two recordings, not only AI fixes. It is a
quick way to check a refactor:

```{r, eval = has_dplyr}
code <- readLines(rewind_example())
code <- sub("amount = as.numeric(amount)",
            "amount = as.numeric(gsub(\"[^0-9.]\", \"\", amount))", code, fixed = TRUE)
new <- rewind_script(text = code, key = "order_id")
compare_traces(tr, new)
attr(compare_traces(tr, new), "issues")
```

## Ship it in a container

`containerize()` reads a script without running it, finds every package it
uses (`library()`, `require()`, `requireNamespace()` and `pkg::fun`), and
writes a Docker recipe:

```{r}
dir <- tempfile("job-")
dir.create(dir)
writeLines(c("library(stats)", "d <- read.csv('sales.csv')", "print(summary(d))"),
           file.path(dir, "job.R"))
writeLines("x,y\n1,2", file.path(dir, "sales.csv"))

containerize(file.path(dir, "job.R"))
cat(readLines(file.path(dir, "container", "Dockerfile")), sep = "\n")
```

The recipe:

* starts from `rocker/r-ver` at your R version;
* installs every package at the version installed on your machine, through
  `pak`, which also installs the system libraries those packages need;
* copies in data files the script reads by relative path;
* runs the script with `Rscript`.

The generated `README.md` has the two commands to build and run it.
`script_packages()` returns just the package list, which is handy for a
`DESCRIPTION` or a lock file.

```{r, include = FALSE}
unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)
```
